behaviour: Unit tests for the pure range model in packages/element/src/textRanges.ts.
rules: 1. Import the functions from "../src/textRanges" and types from "../src/types"; use a FontString like `"10px Cascadia, Segoe UI Emoji" as FontString` with wrapText from "../src/textWrapping" where a wrapped text is needed.
2. Freeze inputs with Object.freeze (array and each range) in at least the apply and shift cases to prove inputs are not mutated.
3. Assert values with toEqual; no snapshots.

tests.name: normalize merges adjacent equal runs
normalize resolves overlaps and clamps
tests.given: overlapping red [0,5) and blue [3,8) plus [-2,1) and [8,99) entries over length 9
tests.expect: sorted, non-overlapping, clamped to [0,9], later entry wins on overlap

tests.name: normalize drops empty, inverted and unstyled ranges
applyStyle colour inside a highlight keeps the highlight
tests.given: highlight yellow [0,10), apply color red to [3,6)

tests.name: applyStyle clearing both attributes removes the range
applyStyle with an empty selection is a no-op
shift: insert before a range
shift: insert inside a range extends it
shift: insert at range start and end stays unstyled
tests.given: range [4,7), insert at 4 and separately at 7

tests.name: shift: insert after a range
shift: delete inside and spanning a range trims it
shift: delete that empties a range drops it
shift: replacement inside a range
split onto wrapped lines with a break inside a styled range
tests.given: originalText 'Hello Excalidraw world' wrapped at 100 (break drops a space), red over 'Excalidraw wo'
tests.expect: each line's run texts concatenate to the line; red runs cover exactly the styled characters on both lines

tests.name: split keeps hard line breaks
restoreStyleRanges drops invalid entries and clamps
restoreStyleRanges returns undefined for legacy/invalid input
withStyleRanges omits the key for an empty list and bumps the version
tests.given: a text element with ranges, set []
tests.expect: no 'styleRanges' key (`'styleRanges' in el` false), version + 1; setting an equal list returns the same object

style_from.reason: pure unit test layout in packages/element/tests

uses.reason: API.createElement for a text element in the withStyleRanges case

behaviour: Adds a describe block checking that styled runs follow wrapText output across re-wraps at different widths.
rules: 1. Add `import { splitRangesIntoLines } from "../src/textRanges";` after the ../src/textWrapping import.
2. New top-level describe "splitRangesIntoLines with wrapText" appended at the end of the file.

tests.name: runs cover the same characters at every wrap width
tests.given: originalText 'Bid request timeout 120ms' with red on '120ms', wrapped by wrapText at widths 60, 120 and Infinity
tests.expect: for each width the concatenated runs equal the wrapped lines and the red runs join to '120ms'

tests.name: whitespace dropped at a break does not shift styles
tests.given: text with several spaces at the break point and a highlight right after it
tests.expect: the highlighted run text equals the styled original substring

behaviour: Adds element-level tests that ranges survive binding into a container, font family and font size changes, and re-wrap.
rules: 1. Import newTextElement from "../src/newElement", getStyledTextLines from "../src/textRanges" and redrawTextBoundingBox from "../src/textElement" (extend the existing ../src/textElement import list).

2. Append a top-level describe "style ranges" at the end of the file; build elements with newTextElement / API.createElement and change them with newElementWith or a Scene from @excalidraw/element where a container is needed.

tests.name: newTextElement omits styleRanges when none are given
tests.given: newTextElement({ text: 'hi', x: 0, y: 0 }) and the same with styleRanges: []
tests.expect: `'styleRanges' in el` is false for both

tests.name: newTextElement normalizes given ranges
ranges survive font family and size changes
tests.given: a styled text, then newElementWith(el, { fontSize: 40, fontFamily: FONT_FAMILY.Nunito })
tests.expect: styleRanges deep-equal the original; getStyledTextLines still covers the same characters

tests.name: ranges survive binding into a container and re-wrap
tests.given: a styled text bound to a narrow rectangle via redrawTextBoundingBox so text wraps
tests.expect: styleRanges unchanged; joined run texts per line equal the wrapped lines

sites.rule: rule 1: add redrawTextBoundingBox to the list, and the two new import lines after it

behaviour: Adds restore tests for styleRanges: legacy text has no key, invalid entries dropped, out-of-bounds clamped, valid ranges round-trip through serializeAsJSON.
rules: 1. Insert the cases inside describe("restoreElements") after the 'should not delete empty text element…' case; build input with API.createElement({ type: "text", text: ... }) and assign styleRanges through a cast to any.
2. Assert with `'styleRanges' in restored` and toEqual, never snapshots.

tests.name: legacy text element restores without styleRanges
tests.given: a text element with no styleRanges key
tests.expect: restored element has no styleRanges key

tests.name: invalid styleRanges are dropped
out-of-bounds styleRanges are clamped
valid styleRanges round-trip through serializeAsJSON
tests.given: a styled text serialized with serializeAsJSON then parsed and restored

behaviour: Adds a concurrent-edit case: two versions of one text with different text and ranges reconcile to the same winner on both sides, carrying that winner's ranges.
rules: 1. Import API from "../helpers/api" and withStyleRanges, applyStyle from "@excalidraw/element".

2. Build a base text element, then a local and a remote version (each newElementWith new originalText/text plus withStyleRanges), giving the remote a higher version; call reconcileElements(local, remote, {} as AppState) and reconcileElements(remote, local, {} as AppState).
3. Append the case inside describe("elements reconciliation") before its closing line.

tests.name: concurrent text edits keep text and ranges from the same version
tests.given: local 'abc def' with red [0,3) (version 3) vs remote 'abc XYZ def' with highlight [4,7) (version 4)
tests.expect: both reconciliations return the remote element, whose originalText and styleRanges belong together

sites.rule: rule 1: the @excalidraw/element value import (keep it separate); the ../helpers/api import goes after the ../../data/reconcile import via S2
